chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim Majilawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hannan ibn Sudair, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, climbed the pulpit on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, and then he said: O people, indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has certainly removed from you the vanity of the Jahiliya and its pride with its fathers. Alas, you are from Adam, and Adam is from mud, and the best of the servants of Allah to Him is the one among them who is most God-fearing. Indeed, Arabic is not a begetting father or mother, but a speaking tongue. Hence, the one whose action reaches short, the satisfaction of Allah will not make him reach his dignity. Alas, every blood [debt] that was during the Jahiliya, or hatred, it is under these two feet of mine until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about tribal pride and blood debts on the Day of Conquest of Mecca?
ai.summary: Delivered at the pivotal moment of the Conquest of Mecca, this sermon by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet's dismantling of the pre-Islamic tribal hierarchy (nakhwa) by grounding human worth in piety (taqwa) rather than lineage or linguistic fluency. The declaration that all pre-Islamic blood debts and grudges are nullified signifies a comprehensive social reset, establishing a new egalitarian order under divine authority. This event is central to Shia historiography as it marks the transition from tribal allegiance to universal Islamic brotherhood.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem Majilawayh, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammed bin Sinan, from Hannan bin Sudair, from his father, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, climbed the pulpit on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, and then he said: O people, indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has certainly removed from you the vanity of the Jahiliya and its (act of expressing) pride with its fathers. Alas, you are, indeed, from Adam, and Adam is (made) from mud, and the best of the servants of Allah to Him is the one among them who is most godfearing. Indeed, the Arabic is not a begetting father, however, it is a speaking tongue. Hence, the one whose action reaches short, the satisfaction of Allah will not make him reach his dignity. Alas, every blood, indeed, that was during the Jahiliya, or hatred, it is under these two feet of mine until the Day of Resurrection.
